counties.notes: East Baton Rouge Parish (Baton Rouge, pop. 456,000; state capital) Tax Parcel layer. Louisiana uses 'parish' instead of 'county'. East Baton Rouge Parish is the combined city/parish government. 21 fields confirmed: ID, ASSESSMENT_NUM, PRONO, OWNER, OWNER_ADDRESS, OWNER_CITY_STATE_ZIP, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS, SUBDIVISION, WARD_SECTION, LOT, BLOCK, LEGAL_DESCRIPTION, FLOOD_ZONE, SALE_YEAR, STATUS, SUM_HOMESTEAD_EXEMPTION, SUM_LOT_VALUE, SUM_LAND_VALUE, SUM_IMPROVEMENT_VALUE, SUM_FAIR_MARKET_VALUE, SUM_ASSESSED_VALUE. Verified 2026-05-15: SMITH returns Baton Rouge addresses (e.g., '12523 MERLIN AVE', '9758 W TAMS DR'). EBRGIS manages 200+ public datasets.

searchFields.label: GeoPIN (lot id, shared by condo units)

contact.department: City of New Orleans GIS (NOLA GIS)

counties.notes: LIVE 2026-10-03 for lookup by location in clients that complete the TLS chain (see TLS below); no attribute search. Layer 15 refuses any query that NAMES its outFields except an exact PARCELID equality: measured 2026-10-03 on the paid shapes (point + 30 m buffer; 800 m envelope with geometry) and on a scan (OBJECTID>0, resultRecordCount=1), every named column list answers HTTP 200 carrying ArcGIS error 400 "Failed to execute query." in about 0.2 s, while the identical request with outFields=* answers 40 features in 0.28 s and 501 features (957 KB) in 0.65 s. UrbanKit sends outFields=* to this layer (api/_lib/arcgis-quirks.ts, WILDCARD_OUT_FIELDS) and keeps only the role columns. Any predicate that scans the table (1=1, OBJECTID>0, PARCELID IS NOT NULL, an owner LIKE) runs past 40 s even for a single row, so no where-clause search is offered (attributeSearch: unsupported) and owner-name lookup is not available here; the owner columns (OWNERNME1, OWNERNME2) and the mailing address (PSTLADDRESS, PSTLCITY, PSTLSTATE, PSTLZIP5) are returned on every spatial hit (a UrbanKit row keeps PSTLADDRESS, the street line). IDS: PARID is the assessor's per-unit parcel id (e.g. 622-SALEXANDERST) and is listed first so rows key by unit; PARCELID is the GeoPIN, a lot id shared by every condo unit on the lot (a 30 m buffer in the CBD: 40 units, 3 lots, 39 owners), so keying on it would collapse a notice list to one row per lot; TAXBILLID is the tax bill number. Exact PARCELID equality answers in 0.2 s and is the sample query, which is also the predicate the liveness probe falls back to when its first shape (1=1) times out. CORS reflects the request origin. TLS: the server sends an INCOMPLETE certificate chain (leaf without its Sectigo intermediate). Clients that fetch the missing intermediate themselves (curl on Windows, Chromium and Safari through the OS store) connect; Node's fetch fails the handshake with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE (measured 2026-10-04). UrbanKit's billed bulk-enrichment and radius paths run on Vercel's Edge runtime, which cannot be given a certificate authority and whose handling of an incomplete chain is undocumented and not yet measured, so assume they cannot serve this parish until a keyed test on the deployed function shows otherwise; today an Orleans row ends county-unavailable and is refunded, unchanged from before. The liveness probe pins the intermediate, so its ok reflects the layer, not the paid paths. An agent that fetches this URL from Node must trust the Sectigo intermediate or the request fails before any query runs. Tracked in GitHub issue #906. HISTORY: marked unreachable 2026-08-29 after 463 consecutive failed probes whose predicate (PARCELID IS NOT NULL) is a table scan; the layer was answering spatial queries the whole time. Ownership data looked dated during the 2026-08 checks; the 2026-10-03 rows carry current-looking owner names.
